# Documentation replay inputs

Synthetic maintenance metadata for issue #105, authored from this checkout's public documentation and fixtures. No private consumer content was imported.

`examples.json` is a closed repository-maintenance format, not an application contract. Each identified P0 command block binds its exact displayed argv, fixture, required lane, exit/stream and independent semantic check in `scripts/test-docs-examples.mjs`. Setup blocks describe visible prerequisite provisioning; the gate never builds or installs silently. Unclassified blocks, unknown runners, missing fixtures/dependencies and stale commands fail.

Portable replay uses the existing synthetic minimal/contracted/trace/planner corpus and the NEW MySQL consumer. Planner replay requires the committed Composer lock and pinned TS/Vue tools. MySQL replay requires the committed npm lock and an isolated actual MySQL 8.4 service. Every lane copies its inputs into bounded owned temporary directories, checks source preservation and emits only role-neutral counts. Native checks cannot be satisfied by SQLite, scanner declarations or fake query results.

The gate also executes refusal and mutation controls, repeated read-only outputs, schema validation and input custody checks. It does not establish remote CI or production consumer acceptance merely by returning a local pass.

The greenfield tutorial's visible C/D working-root links must match `contract-planner` then `inspect-planner` in the registry. C uses the contracted tutorial variant for declaration update, two real tests, expected missing-coverage refusal, test attachment and clean conformance; D uses a separate fresh copy of the original partial projection corpus. Wrong root links, missing root declarations and reversed replay order fail static validation.
